newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bangladesh oilseed output seen staying stagnant.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh oilseed output seen staying stagnant.

text.p: Oilseed production in Bangladesh will grow by a meagre 1.0 percent per annum while imports of oils will likely grow by 25,000 tonnes annually, an Indian industry analyst said on Thursday.

G.K. Sood told an Asia Oilseeds conference in Singapore that significant increases in oilseed production in Bangladesh "is not expected due to climatic constraints and relative prices of competing crops."
Production of vegetable oils in 1996/97 October/November will likely be steady at 175,000 tonnes while demand for the same period is seen reaching 590,000 tonnes.
The gap is made up through imports. Soybean oil makes up 200,000 tonnes and palm oil imports reach 150,000 tonnes. The rest of the imports, including rapeseed oil, reaches 65,000 tonnes.
"It will reasonable to expect an increase in the country's oil import needs by about 25,000 tonnes annually for the next few years," Sood said.

He said the proximity of palm supply sources in Indonesia and Malaysia, the two leading producers of palm oil in the world, will make it likely that Bangladesh buyers will source their oils from the two countries.
